title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description:
A binary search tree (BST) requires that, for every node, all values in its left sub-tree are strictly smaller and all values in its right sub-tree are strictly larger than the node's value. Decide whether the given tree is a valid BST.

Input format
One line: the tree in level-order, values separated by spaces, with the word null for a missing child. Children of null nodes are not listed (the usual level-order serialisation). For example "3 9 20 null null 15 7".

Output format
YES if the tree is a valid BST, otherwise NO.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes <= 100000. Values fit in a 32-bit signed integer. An empty tree (token null) is a valid BST.
hints: Checking only that each node is greater than its left child and smaller than its right child is not enough. Why?
Every node must lie within a range (low, high) inherited from all of its ancestors. Passing those bounds down while recursing checks the whole condition.
Alternatively, an in-order traversal of a valid BST visits values in strictly increasing order. Duplicates make the tree invalid.

examples.explanation: The right child 4 is smaller than the root 5, so this is not a BST.
